display_title: Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout to 3D ragged_dot args and outputs

head_commit.message:
Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout to 3D ragged_dot args and outputs

Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout from chlo.ragged_dot to 3D arguments and
outputs

* Layout pullback through transpose: When a 3D operand is transposed via
  `{0, 2, 1}` before entering `chlo.ragged_dot` (which requires `{2, 1, 0}`),
  the pre-transpose tensor's required minor-to-major layout is pulled back
  via $M_X[k] = P[M_Y[k]]$, resulting in `{1, 2, 0}`.
* Precise operand seeding: In `chlo.ragged_dot`, only the RHS operand (operand
  1) is seeded with `{2, 1, 0}` when its rank is 3 and
  `rhs_group_dimensions[0] == 0`. The LHS operand (operand 0) is never
  seeded. 3D results are seeded with `{2, 1, 0}` where applicable.
* Concurrency, thread safety, and buffer adoption: When a 3D parameter
  requires relayout in `EnqueueExecutable`, both the relayout buffer and the
  parameter buffer are fully synchronized via `Synchronize()` prior to adoption,
  guaranteeing that no device or worker execution reading either buffer is in
  flight. In `DeviceBufferList::Data`, buffer access and replacement in
  `materialized_buffers_` is strictly protected by `mutable absl::Mutex
  buffers_mutex_`. `DeviceBufferList::AdoptMaterializedBufferFrom` atomically
  replaces the parameter's underlying buffer with the relayout buffer while
  updating its shape layout to the target layout under `mutex_`. Adopting the
  relayout buffer drops `DeviceBufferList`'s `std::shared_ptr` to the old
  default-layout buffer, releasing it from device HBM so that live buffer
  count/bytes do not double. Subsequent execution steps see that the parameter
  buffer already has the target layout, completely bypassing relayout and
  reusing the adopted buffer directly.
* Output layout propagation on cache hits: `ExecutionTask::FromTraversal`
  stamps non-default output layouts from
  `LoadedExecutableWithMetadata::output_shapes()` onto traversal outputs
  unconditionally, ensuring output layout metadata is preserved on both
  compilation cache misses and cache hits.
* Selective layout recording: In `LoadedExecutableWithMetadata::MakeShared`,
  output layouts that match client defaults are cleared (`clear_layout()`), so
  only non-default output layouts are stamped onto outputs, and only 3D
  parameters whose layout differs from client default are recorded in
  `non_default_3d_param_layouts`.
* Thread-safe relayout buffer caching and reuse: An `absl::Mutex`-guarded
  per-`DeviceBufferList` relayout cache keyed by target `minor_to_major` layout
  and slot index caches unadopted relayout buffers. Modifying or invalidating
  the underlying buffer (`SetAsMaterialized`, `SetAsPendingMaterialization`,
  `SetAsError`, or `AdoptMaterializedBufferFrom`) clears the cache.

name: CI
display_title: [IFRT IR] Add IfrtCallDedupPass to deduplicate CallOp operands and results

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Add IfrtCallDedupPass to deduplicate CallOp operands and results

Imported IFRT IR programs frequently pass the same `!ifrt.array` multiple times to an `ifrt.Call` or return the same value across multiple `ifrt.Call` outputs, inflating atom program signatures and redundant cross-call dataflow.

`IfrtCallDedupPass` processes `ifrt.Call` ops in program order so deduplicated producer outputs cascade into downstream consumer calls in a single pass, leaving dead operands and results to be pruned by `IfrtDcePass`.

For each call, non-donated, non-aliased duplicate inputs with matching callee argument types and normalized argument attributes are merged by redirecting duplicate block arguments inside the callee to the first matching argument. When the callee is non-private or referenced by any other symbol user—such as another `ifrt.Call` or an internal `func.call` helper—the pass clones and privatizes it before mutating its arguments.

After merging duplicate inputs, caller uses of duplicate outputs returning the same callee value with identical `!ifrt.array` types and result attributes are redirected to the first matching output. Outputs aliased to an input of the call or donated/aliased to a downstream consumer (e.g. aliasing or donating `ifrt.CopyArrays`) are kept isolated so deduplication cannot introduce double-donation or unintended buffer aliasing.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1016581125

name: CI
display_title: `MemoryUsageTracker::PickRematerializationCandidates` spends up to 40s on large SPMD modules when memory stays above the target limit across thousands of program points. On each express lane candidate, `GetCostOfCompression` called `GetShapeSize` three times on original and compact layouts even when the output was already dead. `HloRematInstructionList::GetItem` also performed pointer hash lookups into heap allocated items on every user and liveness query.

head_commit.message:
`MemoryUsageTracker::PickRematerializationCandidates` spends up to 40s on large SPMD modules when memory stays above the target limit across thousands of program points. On each express lane candidate, `GetCostOfCompression` called `GetShapeSize` three times on original and compact layouts even when the output was already dead. `HloRematInstructionList::GetItem` also performed pointer hash lookups into heap allocated items on every user and liveness query.

Cache both the compact shape and its byte sizes per instruction, and check output liveness before querying compact layout information. Store `HloRematItem` nodes in `std::deque` with direct `local_id` indexing and cache rematerializability and overwrite flags on each item. Exclude dead, denylisted, pinned, and nonrematerializable items from the express lane, and avoid per candidate vector allocations when `max_block_size` is 1. Rematerialization decisions, schedules, and peak memory are unchanged.

| Benchmark | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `BM_PickRematerializationCandidates/256` | 58.37 ms | 10.24 ms | 5.70x |
| `BM_PickRematerializationCandidates/1024` | 909.30 ms | 123.00 ms | 7.39x |

Tests:
- `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:hlo_rematerialization_test`: pins compact shape and size memoization, cache growth stability, express lane filtering, peak priority dead user removal, and `BM_PickRematerializationCandidates`.

name: CI
display_title: [StreamExecutor] Serialize cuStreamWaitEvent and cuGraphLaunch on CudaStream

head_commit.message:
[StreamExecutor] Serialize cuStreamWaitEvent and cuGraphLaunch on CudaStream

Fixes #52488

When multiple host threads dispatch to the same GPU device (such as in PJRT
sharing compute_stream()), concurrent execution of cuGraphLaunch and
cuStreamWaitEvent on the same CUstream can trigger a race condition in the
CUDA driver where cuStreamWaitEvent is silently dropped. This causes
downstream consumer kernels to execute before awaited work (such as NCCL
collectives or host-to-device transfers) has finished, resulting in silent data
corruption.

Serialize cuStreamWaitEvent and cuGraphLaunch on the same CudaStream using a
per-stream absl::Mutex to eliminate the driver race without synchronizing the
device or degrading throughput.

head_commit.message:
Keep AlgebraicSimplifier from rewriting division by a power and NaN-unsafe compares

Rewriting A / pow(B, C) as A * pow(B, -C) changes results, so only do it
with fast math. Folding x >= 0 to true for a non-negative x is wrong when
x can be NaN, so restrict those compare folds to integral types.

Fixes #52418
Fixes #52417

x can be NaN, so restrict those compare folds to integral types.

Fixes #52418
Fixes #52417

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

TreeReductionRewriter splits large reductions into a reduce-window followed by
a reduce. CPU fusion did not accept kReduceWindow, so the input of the
reduce-window was always materialized.

Allow fusing producers into a reduce-window if its windows do not overlap and
are not dilated, so every input element is read once. A reduce-window is never
fused into its consumer. Make ReusesOperandElements return false for the array
operands of such a reduce-window, as it already does for kReduce. Also treat a
max reduce-window like a max reduce when looking for the softmax shift pattern.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Require K>=32 for 8-bit Triton dot operands on CUDA

NVIDIA 8-bit MMA uses K=32. The Triton search space allowed 16, which produced 2x results. Enforce 32 in the search space and both verifiers, and reject smaller explicit configs. Bump the Triton and autotune cache versions.

name: CI
display_title: [hlo_runner] Support `xla.sdy.use_tuple_args` modules and pre-flattened arguments in FunctionalHloRunner.

head_commit.message:
[hlo_runner] Support `xla.sdy.use_tuple_args` modules and pre-flattened arguments in FunctionalHloRunner.

JAX defers the tupling of large argument lists to the ShardyXLA pass through the `xla.sdy.use_tuple_args` frontend attribute, so the compiled executable takes a single tuple parameter although the unoptimized HLO module has one parameter per argument. FunctionalHloRunner derived `parameter_is_tupled_arguments` from the entry signature of the input module and therefore disagreed with the executable when such a module was compiled with Shardy enabled.

`CompleteCompileOptions` now also sets `parameter_is_tupled_arguments` when the module carries `xla.sdy.use_tuple_args` and the ShardyXLA pass will run, and `Run` accepts per-device argument lists that are already flattened (one literal per tuple leaf) for executables with a tuple parameter. Covered by a new FunctionalHloRunnerTest case on CPU.

  ROCm client passes the allocator config's, as for the default pool, so
  allocator memory registration also sees the temp pool's regions.
- Document at the call site and in the flag's help that next to a
  preallocated default pool without spatial partitioning, the separate
  collective pool gets the same limit as the temp pool and both take
  from the same remaining device memory.
- Test that the temp pool reports its regions to the visitors.
